Classificazione di Stanford: tipo A se è:
Stanford classification: type A if the ascending aorta is involved (urgent surgical indication), type B if the dissection begins after the origin of the left subclavian artery (DeBakey III). The TEM classification (Type, Entry, Malperfusion) adds the site of the entry tear and organ malperfusion.
Distinguishing the lumens: the true lumen continues in continuity with the non-dissected aorta, is usually smaller and in the arterial phase is denser; the false lumen is larger, forms an acute angle with the flap (beak sign), may contain thin filaments (cobweb) and opacify late or thrombose.
In the report: proximal and distal extent, maximum aortic diameter, from which lumen the celiac trunk, superior mesenteric artery and renal arteries arise, perfusion of bowel and kidneys, signs of rupture (pleural or mediastinal effusion, periaortic hematoma).
Complications that change management in type B: malperfusion, rupture or impending rupture, refractory pain or hypertension, aortic diameter ≥ 55 mm or rapid growth; risk factors for aneurysmal evolution: initial diameter > 40 mm, large or partially thrombosed false lumen.
In this case: classic type B with both lumens patent; the flap spirals (the false lumen passes from left-posterior to anterior in the abdomen) and the visceral branches arise from different lumens.
